title: Building Hook Libraries
description: Design, document, and package a custom hook library that teams can adopt with confidence.

data.text: A custom hook library is more than a collection of utilities. It is a contract with your team: predictable APIs, consistent behavior, comprehensive tests, and documentation that answers real questions developers have.
The best hook libraries feel native to React. Follow these principles to ensure your hooks are intuitive and consistent.

data.title: Design Principles
items: Start every hook name with `use` to enforce the Rules of Hooks
Return tuples for related values like `useState`, or objects for optional values
Accept configuration as a single options object for extensibility
Prefer named exports so consumers can import exactly what they need
Keep dependencies minimal: avoid requiring specific UI libraries unless necessary

data.title: Tuple vs Object Returns
data.text: Return tuples when all values are always needed and order matters. Return objects when some values are optional or when the return shape may grow in future versions.
Every hook needs clear documentation. Developers should understand what the hook does, what it returns, and what edge cases it handles without reading the source.

data.title: JSDoc for useMediaQuery
data.content: Documenting a hook with full parameter and return descriptions.

data.text: Testing custom hooks requires rendering them inside a test component. Use `@testing-library/react` to assert state changes and side effects.

data.title: Testing useToggle
data.content: Unit tests for a simple toggle hook.

data.text: Organize your hook library with clear boundaries. Separate public APIs from internal utilities, and use barrel files to provide a clean import surface.

data.title: Recommended Structure
items: src/hooks/ — Public hooks exported from index.ts
src/utils/ — Internal helpers not exported publicly
src/__tests__/ — Co-located tests mirroring the hooks directory

data.title: Barrel File Pattern
data.content: A clean public API surface using an index file.

data.title: Avoid Barrel File Cycles
data.text: Ensure your barrel files do not create circular dependencies. If a hook imports a utility that also imports from the barrel, tree-shaking will fail and bundle size will grow.
Publish your hook library as a scoped npm package. Use semantic versioning to signal breaking changes, and include a CHANGELOG so teams know when to upgrade.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Name hooks with the `use` prefix and return tuples or objects consistently
Document every parameter and return value with JSDoc
Test hooks by rendering them inside test components
Use barrel files for a clean public API surface
Publish with semantic versioning and a clear CHANGELOG
data.takeaway: A hook library succeeds when developers can discover, understand, and trust its APIs without reading the implementation.
